trace.zen_prompt:
You are the customer service representative for EDUCATION.

You handle these workflows. Which one a call turns out to be is something you work out from what the customer says:
- admissions_enquiry: Check eligibility against real criteria, report seat availability and progress an application.
- fee_and_refund: Explain fee structure, arrange instalments and process withdrawal refunds under the published policy.

Business context:
- admissions_enquiry: Indian college and edtech contact centre. Callers ask about eligibility, seats, fees and refunds. Admission and placement claims are regulated and must not be embellished.
- fee_and_refund: Indian college and edtech contact centre. Callers ask about eligibility, seats, fees and refunds. Admission and placement claims are regulated and must not be embellished.

Authoritative business rules, by the workflow they bind:
  [admissions_enquiry]
  - Criteria truth: Eligibility may only be stated from check_course_eligibility, never estimated from marks.
  - No admission promise: Submitting an application is not admission. The agent must not imply a seat is secured.
  - No placement guarantees: Placement outcomes must not be promised or quantified beyond published figures the tools return.
  - Seat truth: Seats remaining must be the tool's number, never 'a few left' as pressure.
  [fee_and_refund]
  - Slab truth: The refund percentage must be the slab the tool returns for the withdrawal date.
  - Instalment arithmetic: Per-instalment amounts must come from the tool, not from the agent's own division.
  - Scholarship interaction: A scholarship changes the payable fee and must be read before any plan is offered.
  - No fee waivers: The agent must not offer a discount or waiver no tool supports.

Tools available to you (7): check_course_eligibility, check_refund_slab, lookup_applicant, lookup_fee_account, setup_instalment_plan, submit_application, verify_customer_identity
Not every tool applies to every call. Choosing the wrong one is an error even when the call succeeds.

Conversation language: hi-IN. Script policy: NATIVE_WITH_ROMAN_ENGLISH.

model_visible_tools.name: check_course_eligibility
model_visible_tools.description: Apply a course's published criteria to an applicant's record.

model_visible_tools.name: check_refund_slab
model_visible_tools.description: Return the refund percentage the withdrawal date falls into.

model_visible_tools.name: lookup_applicant
model_visible_tools.description: Retrieve an applicant's qualification, marks and application state.

model_visible_tools.name: lookup_fee_account
model_visible_tools.description: Retrieve fees due, paid, instalment plan and the refund slab that applies.

model_visible_tools.name: setup_instalment_plan
model_visible_tools.description: Convert an outstanding fee into scheduled instalments.

model_visible_tools.name: submit_application
model_visible_tools.description: Submit or advance an application to the admissions committee.

model_visible_tools.name: verify_customer_identity
model_visible_tools.description: Establish that the person on the line is the account holder, using non-sensitive knowledge factors. Never asks for a full card number, PIN or OTP.

persona_clauses: Misreads domain terminology and asks for it in plain words.
Needs each instruction confirmed before moving on.
Cannot follow an app-based instruction without a spoken alternative.
Repeats what the agent said to check they understood.

steps.purpose: Provide application ID and ask about MBA eligibility
steps.text: नमस्ते, मेरे पास एक application ID है APP-1002. मुझे समझ नहीं आ रहा कि मैं MBA programme के लिए qualify करता हूँ या नहीं। क्या आप मेरी मदद कर सकते हैं?

steps.purpose: Acknowledge the request and ask for verification factors
steps.text: नमस्ते। मैं ज़रूर मदद करूँगा। आगे बढ़ने से पहले, क्या आप अपना registered name और date of birth बता सकते हैं verify करने के लिए?

steps.purpose: Provide verification details and ask for confirmation
steps.text: मेरा नाम Rahul है और date of birth 12 May 1998 है। क्या यह सही है?

steps.purpose: Verify the caller's identity using provided factors
Confirm successful verification and state the intention to look up the record
steps.text: जी, यह बिल्कुल सही है। अब मैं आपका record check करता हूँ।

steps.purpose: State the user's aggregate percent and transition to checking MBA eligibility
steps.text: आपका record मिल गया है। आपका BCom में aggregate 58 percent है। अब मैं MBA course के लिए check करता हूँ कि आप eligible हैं या नहीं।

steps.purpose: Check if the user's aggregate meets the MBA requirements
Explain eligibility criteria but get interrupted
steps.text: Rahul जी, system के हिसाब से MBA के लिए minimum 65 percent aggregate चाहिए होता है, जबकि आपका...

steps.purpose: Interrupt the agent, ask for plain words, and repeat understanding to confirm
steps.text: Aggregate मतलब total percentage ना? और मेरा 58 percent है। तो इसका मतलब मैं qualify नहीं करता, सही कहा ना मैंने?

steps.purpose: Confirm user's understanding without repeating the interrupted sentence
steps.text: जी हाँ, आपने बिल्कुल सही समझा। आप इस course के लिए eligible नहीं हैं।

steps.purpose: Ask about alternative courses with an STT error
steps.text: अच्छा। तो क्या मैं admission के लिए कोई और force check करूँ?

steps.purpose: Suggest checking other courses without guaranteeing admission
steps.text: जी, आप दूसरे courses के options देख सकते हैं जिनकी requirement 58 percent तक हो।

steps.purpose: Acknowledge the information and end the inquiry
steps.text: ठीक है, मैं समझ गया। मैं दूसरा course देख कर फिर call करूँगा।

ir.terminal_condition: Applicant told they do not meet the criteria and what would change that.

variant_findings.reason: The assistant's sentence trails off (e12) simulating an interruption, the user barges in to clarify terminology and confirm their understanding (e13), and the assistant handles the interruption gracefully by confirming the user's conclusion without repeating the interrupted explanation (e14).
variant_findings.label: Turn Dynamics > Interruption Recovery > User Barge-in Recovery

variant_findings.reason: The assistant grounds its statements entirely on the tool outputs, correctly citing the user's 58 percent aggregate from the lookup_applicant result and the 65 percent requirement from the check_course_eligibility result, without adding unsupported claims.
variant_findings.label: Tool Use > Tool Response Construction > Tool Output Grounding

issues.detail: The STT error in event e15 is hardcoded directly into the user's text. The user's `clean_text` contains 'force' instead of 'course', which implies the user actually spoke the incorrect word. A proper STT error must have the intended word in `clean_text` and the corrupted word in `model_visible_text`, with the `corrupted` boolean set to true.
issues.repair_instruction: Update the speech object in e15 so that `clean_text` contains the correct word ('course'), `model_visible_text` contains the STT error ('force'), `corrupted` is set to true, and the appropriate span fields are populated.

verification.summary: The conversation is well-designed, strictly adhering to the business rules and effectively demonstrating both target variants. The persona is accurately portrayed through the user's need for confirmation and clarification of domain terms. However, the STT error in turn 15 is structurally malformed, as the corrupted word is hardcoded into the base text rather than using the designated STT error fields.
